description: Replace/adapt the auth test suite to reflect the new role-based authorization model, and document the Google OAuth setup (env vars, Google Cloud consent screen + credentials, redirect URIs, role assignment) in web/.env.example and web/README.md. Keeps the Vitest suite green and meaningful, and gives the user everything needed to configure OAuth in Google Cloud + Vercel.
steps: Rewrite web/tests/staff-auth.test.ts (rename to web/tests/auth-roles.test.ts if clearer) to test the new model with real assertions that would fail if the logic were reverted: (a) resolveRoleForEmail returns the seed role for a DEFAULT_USERS email, honors ADMIN_EMAILS/TEST_ADMIN_EMAILS/REPORT_REVIEWER_EMAILS allowlists (set/unset via process.env in the test with cleanup in afterEach like the existing test does for STAFF_ACCESS_TOKEN), and defaults to STUDENT for unknown emails; (b) isStaffRole is true for SUPER_ADMIN/TEST_ADMIN/REPORT_REVIEWER and false for STUDENT; (c) isAuthConfigured reflects presence/absence of GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET/AUTH_SECRET; (d) the role-based authorizeStaff/requireRole helper allows a staff user and rejects a student/anonymous, and (if kept) the STAFF_ACCESS_TOKEN legacy fallback still works only when auth is unconfigured. Do NOT test framework internals of NextAuth; test the project's own pure functions. Ensure the file is picked up by vitest.config.ts (tests/**/*.test.ts).
Confirm the full suite passes: from web/ run `npm run test -- --run`. Adjust any other test affected by the refactor. The suite must remain green.

Update web/.env.example: add and document the new required-at-runtime vars — GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, AUTH_SECRET (and AUTH_URL/NEXTAUTH_URL if your chosen NextAuth version needs it in production; Auth.js v5 infers URL on Vercel but document setting AUTH_URL for other hosts). Add ADMIN_EMAILS, TEST_ADMIN_EMAILS, REPORT_REVIEWER_EMAILS (comma-separated allowlists) with Spanish comments explaining role assignment. Note all are OPTIONAL for `next build` (read at runtime) and that without them auth runs 'no configurado' / demo mode. Update the STAFF_ACCESS_TOKEN comment to describe it as an optional local/demo fallback superseded by Google OAuth.

Update web/README.md 'Autenticación y autorización' section (currently around lines 34-60): document that Google OAuth (Auth.js/NextAuth) is now the real sign-in and the primary authorization gate; describe how roles are assigned (seed users by email, then ADMIN_EMAILS/TEST_ADMIN_EMAILS/REPORT_REVIEWER_EMAILS allowlists, default STUDENT) and HOW TO MAKE SOMEONE AN ADMIN (add their Google email to ADMIN_EMAILS). Provide the Google Cloud setup steps: create OAuth consent screen, create OAuth 2.0 Client ID (Web application), and set Authorized redirect URIs to `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/google` (local) and `https://<tu-app>.vercel.app/api/auth/callback/google` (prod). List the exact env vars to set locally in web/.env.local and in Vercel Project Settings. Explain the build-safety property (build needs no secrets) and that STAFF_ACCESS_TOKEN is now only an optional local/demo fallback. Keep all prose in Spanish.
acceptance_criteria: The auth test file exercises resolveRoleForEmail, isStaffRole, isAuthConfigured and the role-based authorization helper with assertions that fail if the implementation is reverted.
`npm run test -- --run` passes (suite green, count >= previous meaningful coverage).
web/.env.example documents GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, AUTH_SECRET, the *_EMAILS allowlists, and clarifies STAFF_ACCESS_TOKEN is an optional fallback, all in Spanish.

web/README.md 'Autenticación y autorización' explains Google OAuth as the real gate, role assignment, how to make an admin, Google Cloud redirect URIs (local + Vercel), and the build-safety note, in Spanish.
verification: From web/: run `npm run test -- --run` and confirm all tests pass.
From web/: run `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` and confirm both pass.
From web/: run `env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" npm run build` and confirm the build succeeds with no env vars.
findings: Replaced web/tests/staff-auth.test.ts with web/tests/auth-roles.test.ts (still matched by tests/**/*.test.ts). Suite grew from 53 to 68 tests, all green. New tests cover: resolveRoleForEmail (seed-user precedence, ADMIN/TEST_ADMIN/REPORT_REVIEWER allowlists, comma/space separators, highest-privilege wins across multiple lists, STUDENT default), isStaffRole (staff roles vs STUDENT), isAuthConfigured (real logic from web/auth.ts), and the role-based guard authorizeStaff/authorizeStaffWithRoles/authorizeStaffRequest (allows correct staff role, rejects student/anonymous, token superseded by OAuth session, and legacy STAFF_ACCESS_TOKEN fallback only when auth unconfigured). Key testing insight: the real web/auth.ts imports next-auth which pulls next/server (unresolvable under vitest node env), so instead of mocking @/auth we mock 'next-auth', 'next-auth/providers/google' and '@/lib/auth/link-user' with minimal stubs, letting us exercise the REAL isAuthConfigured (controlled via env vars) and only mock getCurrentUser from @/lib/auth/session for guard tests. Updated web/.env.example (added GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET, AUTH_SECRET, AUTH_URL/NEXTAUTH_URL note, ADMIN_EMAILS/TEST_ADMIN_EMAILS/REPORT_REVIEWER_EMAILS; reframed STAFF_ACCESS_TOKEN as optional local/demo fallback) and web/README.md (rewrote 'Autenticación y autorización' for Google OAuth as primary gate, role assignment order, how to make an admin, Google Cloud setup + redirect URIs, build-safety note, env-var table). Verification: npm run test -- --run (68 pass), npm run typecheck (pass), npm run lint (pass, next lint deprecation warning only), and env -i clean `npm run build` succeeds with no env vars.
